children: Savers Value Village’s third-quarter net sales rose 8.5% year over year, while the company swung to net income from a year-earlier loss. Growth in the store base and higher comparable-store sales lifted retail sales; improved merchandise costs and lower interest expense helped, while the prior-year period included a much larger debt-extinguishment loss.
¹ Reported as “Net sales”. ² Reported as “Net income (loss)”. ³ Reported as “Net income (loss) per share, diluted”.
: Total comparable-store sales increased 4.2%, driven primarily by higher average basket and, to a lesser extent, transactions.
: Sales rose 12.2%, with comparable-store sales up 5.9%; segment profit increased 16.2%.
: Sales increased 2.5%, including a 1.5% comparable-store sales gain; segment profit rose 10.0%.
: Processed 298 million pounds, up from 282 million; OSDs and GreenDrop were 82.4% of pounds processed, versus 80.7%.
: Opened 9 stores during the quarter and ended the period with 384 stores.
